name: Tull Varreth
aliases: the fraction the accounts cannot book
the man the board is wrong about

identity.realm: None, and the reason is arithmetic rather than temperament and rather than a refusal. His frame permits both of the two doors the ash belt has open: qi, which is complete and durable in him because it is processed through the same filter as air, and body, which is genuinely dense under load. The mind path is shut outright, the grit having occluded the fine vessels an introspection needs, and that closure is the only one of the three that is anatomical. On this belt the other two are reached the same way by everybody: a dose timed to a tide that will carry it, on a stone bed that holds qi, and the dose is sized against body weight. His weight is not a body weight. The suspended mineral load in his blood counts toward the figure the arithmetic uses, so the number that sizes a dose on any other frame does not resolve on his. Nobody has ever tried it on him, which is the whole of his position: he has not been refused a booking, the booking has no figure to be refused with, and no clerk has ever been in a position to have to admit that. His ceiling is the eighth gate, where the ordinary meridian set ends at the liver, and that ceiling is a chemistry fact rather than a shortage of will.

appearance.presentation: A working man in his late forties, thick through the chest and forearms and narrow everywhere else, built by a decade of carrying stone uphill rather than by any training anybody gave him. He reads as a body that has been worn rather than a body that has been used, and the difference is visible in the way the skin at his collarbone has gone the colour of the rock he works in. He is the only person on the Ore Under the Ash whose airway noise can be heard from the chute mouth, and he has never once tried to soften it, because softening it would mean breathing less.
appearance.age: Forty-nine. Ashwalkers age slowly and this one aged fast for the first twenty years of working, because his intake was a trade rather than a habit, and the trade has been constant since he was nineteen. He does not know his own age on any authority but the roster, and the roster records him as a shift rather than as a man, so the figure has never been checked by anyone with a reason to check it.
appearance.build: Dense and compact, with a permanently dusted coat of mineral across the shoulders and the upper arms that does not brush off and has stopped being washed for. The hands are the striking part: the nails are worn to nothing and the first two joints of the right hand are permanently enlarged from a chute lip he has been gripping since he was nineteen. The frame is heavier than it looks and it does not tire, which is the single most valuable property on this ground and is why nobody here has ever asked him to describe how he feels at the end of a shift.
appearance.complexion: A grey cast under the tan, deeper at the throat and across the shoulders where the air lies. The skin is dry to the point of scaling on the backs of the hands and the sieve itself has dried the tip of his nose permanently, so the upper third of his face carries the roughness of a stone surface and he has simply grown a beard around it. Scarring across the shoulders is old, from a fall of ash he stood in before he understood what standing in a fresh fall means.
appearance.hair: Black going iron at the temples, worn to a stub by a blade he is supposed not to carry underground and which he carries anyway. The hairline has receded two fingers in thirty years. He keeps the beard short with the same blade and does not trim it with any precision, which makes his face the only part of him that is visibly unfinished.
appearance.eyes: Dark, and the only part of this face a person reads first. An ashwalker's smell is gone and what replaced it is a contact sense through the sieve, so his attention goes to surfaces rather than to people, and he is continually startling to talk to because he is looking at the wall behind you while he answers you. There is no second line in them and no warmth that has ever been noted by anybody who was looking for it.
appearance.palette: Ore grey, scoured lichen green and sulphur yellow in the sublimate the coat of the temple's working dress is dyed to, with a hard black at the hands. The grey is not on him so much as ground into the cut of the cloth, and a working garment on this belt is a record of the face and not a choice. There is nothing bright on this ground and nothing on him either.
appearance.attire: Full high collar closed to the jaw, sleeves bound tight at the wrist with a sulphur-cured cord, double-layered at the shoulders because the under-layer is the one that gets replaced and the outer one is the one that gets patched. A short chute apron of hide thick enough to stand on its own, which on the Ore Under the Ash is a working garment and not a costume, and which he has refused three times to have repaired because the repair would be a different hide and the hide is what he stands in. Leggings bound below the knee. Nothing is open anywhere on him and nothing on this ground is cut to be.
appearance.marks: The permanent dust coat is the mark, and the enlarged right-hand joints are the second. Under the jaw and along the inner forearms the skin carries a fine grey stipple that the temple's people call settling and have never once examined, because examining it would require an intake that the body is itself performing. There is no brand and no enrolled mark of any kind on him anywhere, which on this belt is the unusual condition rather than the ordinary one.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried in the way heavy things are unhurried. He leans into a slope rather than stepping up it and will stop mid-sentence to put his mouth to a face of rock and come back to the sentence where he left it, without visibly restarting it. He stands with the wall within reach on one side at all times, which is not a habit, it is what a person who has had a fall of ash in the dark does for a living.

canon.role_in_story: The Ore Under the Ash is the only worked ground on the plains that no institution sells, because the temple forge is public and its ore is entered in the books as spent the moment it comes out of the ground. What no account on this belt has ever managed to book is the fraction that leaves a cut face as air, and Tull works the ground whose entire product is that fraction. He stands at the chute mouth, reads a fall of ash with the sieve in his own face, and says what grade it is; the sieve is the only instrument in the setting that can separate two falls the eye has already agreed are the same, and it is the same organ that turns airborne stone into protein. He is therefore both the reason the belt has a food chain above the lichen and the reason its grinders have air to breathe, and neither job appears in a ledger under his name. He is unaffiliated for a third reason that belongs to neither job: the one booking technology this belt has sizes its dose against body weight, his weight is not a body weight, the figure does not resolve, and nobody has ever tried it on him. Nobody refused him. There is no figure on the form.
canon.first_appearance: Seen at the chute mouth at the change of shift with his mouth against the lip and one hand flat on the wall behind him, telling a hauler that the fall had changed grade within the last hour and that the board still carried the old figure, and that the board would have to be corrected before the shift went down rather than after, because after is the point at which a face has been cut to a number that was already wrong.
canon.lore:
An ashwalker is a body that breathes volcanic grit and keeps it. What makes the species possible is the sieve: a chambered nasal structure lined with cilia that trap grit and pass it into a crop for grinding, so airborne stone becomes protein. Smell is gone and what replaced it is a direct contact sense, which makes this the only population in the record that can tell two ash grades apart by tongue. It is also, on that ground, the entire food chain above the lichen.

The physiology has one long shadow. The mineral load in the blood settles on the liver first, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so the eighth gate is where the whole species stops and stopping is chemistry rather than character. The same grit occludes the fine capillary beds that introspection needs, which is why the mind path is closed to them outright and not merely unpractised. There is no self-audit available to any of them at any stage of a life. What they have instead is a reading of the world that cannot be doubted and cannot be checked, because checking it would require the interior that the grit has already taken.

The ground Tull is on is the third thing. The Ore Under the Ash is held by an institution that does not sell its output at all: the temple forge is public, the ore is booked as spent on extraction, and the only reason the ground is worked is that the working is a rite. What escapes the face is air. The belt's entire airborne load is a working by-product that has never once been entered in any ledger as spent, because no ledger has a column for it and the column is not the shape of the thing: it is neither ore nor spoil nor a crop. It is the raw material of the species, and it is the one figure on the Ironhead Flats that exists in full and is recorded at zero.

This is where his exclusion comes from, and it is not the exclusion anybody on this ground expects. On the belt, the two doors his body permits are opened the same way for everybody: a dose timed to a tide that will carry it, laid on a stone bed that holds qi, with the dose sized against the body it will be given to. The Channel Elixir Method is bought rather than inherited, which makes it the most accessible technology in the setting and the only one that does not require a household. It also requires a weight. A weight is a number a clerk can take off a body, and it is the one measurement on this belt that everybody agrees on, because a weight is a weight. His is not. The suspended mineral in his blood is part of what the scale would report and none of what the arithmetic was derived from, so a figure computed on his frame lands on a number that is wrong by the part of him that is stone, and the method's whole claim is that a figure which is wrong is not a smaller dose but a different preparation. Nobody has tested it. Nobody has any basis for testing it, because the one population that would be the control has a body the control cannot be taken from. He is the setting's standing example of a method that has an untried population and a reason nobody will try, and the reason is written down in the method rather than in him: the arithmetic cannot be trusted on this frame.

What he does about it is unglamorous and has been constant for thirty years. He reads a fall. He tells the shift clerk what grade it is. He does it before the cut goes down rather than after, because after is when the board is already a fact and a face has been opened to it. He is right often enough that the practice has never been questioned and rarely enough that no office has ever been created for it. The temple pays him in the ground's own output, which is to say in the use of a face and not in coin, because coin on this belt would be a figure somebody would eventually ask him to weigh.

What he has wanted, for as long as anyone has asked him, is smaller than a gate and harder than a wage. He wants one office on this belt to write down that his weight is a different substance from everybody else's. It is the only request he has ever made and he has made it four times, to three different clerks and once in writing, and the answer each time was that there is no column for it. He is not refused. There is no column for it. That distinction is the entire architecture of his life and he has never once been able to make a clerk hear it.

There is a bound on it, and it is not him. The temple's books close at the end of each working year, when the forge is read against what came out of the ground, and the close is a physical reading by people with the instruments for it. At that close the fraction that went into the air is either entered or it is not, and there is a clerk whose entire job is to find the discrepancy. He has three attempts left at that reading before the ground is re-templed and the office does not exist. His own measure has a bound too, and he does not discuss it: the load has been in his blood since he was nineteen and it settles on one organ, and there is no technique in the record that slows what it does to that organ.
history: Came onto the Ore Under the Ash at nineteen as a chute hand, having been assessed for the sieve by a man who put a hand of ash on his tongue and moved him to the front of the intake. He has been at the chute mouth for thirty years since, and has not once been moved to a different post, because the post he holds is the only one that requires a person who can read a grade and there is a queue behind him of nobody at all.

Began correcting the fall figure before the cut went down rather than after, in his second working year, and was written down once for it in a hand that was not his own and has since been found twice by people looking for a reason the board was wrong. Both times the correction was right.

Asked, at twenty-six, whether a dose could be sized on him. The clerk who asked did it as a joke about the arithmetic and stopped laughing in the middle of the sentence, and no answer was ever written down, and Tull has been carrying the question since without ever having put it in front of anybody who owed him a reply.

Worked out, somewhere in his thirties, that the airborne fraction is the only figure on this ground that exists in full and is recorded at zero, and began keeping his own count of it against the haulage tonnage, which is the only number the books do carry and which therefore functions as a proxy nobody sanctioned.

This working year, for the fourth time, asked in writing for one office to record that his weight is a different substance from everybody else's, and was told for the fourth time that there is no column for it. Three readings of the forge remain before the ground is re-templed and the office that would have to write it does not exist at all.

personality.summary: Methodical to the point of pedantry about other people's figures and completely unbothered about his own, because he has never had an instrument for the second and has built his whole working life around not needing one. He corrects before rather than after, on the theory that a wrong number costs nothing until somebody acts on it. He is not resentful. He is, in a way that unsettles people, entirely willing.

personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and almost entirely quantitative. He talks in grades, tonnages, hours and orders of change, and when a conversation leaves that territory he returns to it by walking to a wall. Three habits are recorded by different clerks: he says the number first and the reason afterwards, he corrects people by repeating their figure back at them one unit different, and he has never in thirty years used the word 'cultivate' about himself or anybody else on the ground.

relationships.kind: employs every body it takes as a visitor
relationships.note: The guild works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, and the work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body it employs is a visitor. A visitor is present, load-bearing and not a resident, which is a category a person can be in and cannot be entered against. It is why the guild has never questioned his reading and has never created an office for it: there is no line in a visitor's charter to hang one on.

relationships.kind: the case that will be opened in his name and cannot be closed
relationships.note: A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body. His people's dead are the standing instance: a body that is half mineral and half person, in a belt where the frame reads one and the village remembers the other, so the register keeps the assay and the settlement keeps the rest and neither has ever been reconciled against a corpse.

relationships.kind: the instrument and the instrument's inability to check itself
relationships.note: The sieve separates two falls of ash that the eye has already agreed are the same, and it does so by contact rather than by smell, which makes his reading the finest on this ground and entirely unverifiable from inside. The grit that lets him do it has occluded the fine vessels an introspection would need, so he has never once audited a figure in his own life and cannot begin now. The species' single great advantage and its single closed door are the same organ.

reference_stats.summary: A body that does not tire, cannot be frightened, and cannot be posted anywhere the air is not already lethal, holding an instrument that is the finest on the ground and the only one nobody is permitted to check. He has no gate, no reservoir and no technique, and his species' own ceiling is an organ he has been loading since he was nineteen. What he has instead is thirty years of being right on the only measure that governs the ground he stands on, and a figure about himself that has never once resolved.
strengths: a mineral-charged frame that carries load without fatigue and does not slow over a full shift, which on this ground is the property the whole shift rota is written around

carries a suspended particulate load in his blood, which makes him immune to anything airborne that the sieve does not recognise as stone, and gives him a dense frame that does not bruise or cut the way softer tissue does

thirty years of a single reading that has never been found wrong and has been found right twice by people with an interest in it being wrong

one inhalation of a soft airborne toxin is a wound rather than a warning, because there is no second line behind the sieve and no smell to give him the first one
cannot relocate to any ground where the air is survivable, so he is a permanent resident of a workplace that is killing him and cannot be moved off it by anyone

is on the guild's books as a shift rather than as a person, which means there is no line in any charter to hang an office, a seat or a claim on, and nobody has ever had to refuse him anything because there is nothing on the form
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight, and understand why there is none: no gate, no reservoir, no technique, a ceiling that is an organ rather than a wall, and a frame that cannot be exhausted and cannot be frightened. Anything that works on him works by procedure, not by force — a notice, a re-templing, a face closed on a figure he has not read. He will not run and cannot be threatened with anything that requires a person to weigh the threat. The genuinely dangerous thing about him is that he is the only reader on the ground and everybody knows it.
notes: He is unaffiliated, and the ground is the booking arithmetic rather than his body: his frame permits both qi and body and neither is anatomical to him, but the one technology this belt uses to open either door requires a weight that will not resolve on a mineral-charged frame. Nobody refused him. Nobody has ever had a form to refuse him on.
The mind path is shut outright and it is the only one of his three closures that is anatomical: grit in the fine capillary beds. Never write him as someone who might turn inward. He cannot.

Do not write him as a cultivator and do not write him as having declined. He has never been offered a figure and he has never asked for one; the asking he does do is about a column in a ledger, which is a different request entirely.
His ceiling is the eighth gate at the liver and the liver is also what his occupation has been loading for thirty years. That is a fact to write as fact and not as a metaphor.

The grey stipple under his jaw is the species' visible sign and the temple has agreed to call it settling. It is not settling. Nobody has ever looked closely enough to say so, and looking closely would require an intake the body is itself performing.

His one want is a written line saying his weight is a different substance. Three readings of the forge remain before the ground is re-templed and the office that would have to write it does not exist. That is his named bound and it is not him.

art.palette_notes: Ore grey, scoured lichen green and sulphur yellow against basalt and cut rock, with one hard black at the hands and one permanent grey dust-coat across the shoulders and upper arms that does not brush off and is the subject of the art rather than a detail. High collar closed to the jaw, sleeves bound at the wrist, a short hide chute apron thick enough to stand in on its own and repaired never. No glow, no aura, no inner light: nothing on this belt is magic and the picture should refuse the comfort of it. Key light is daylight off a cut face, hard and bouncing, because the whole ground is lit by the thing being worked. Backgrounds are rock, chute lip, timber shoring or open air over a spoil fan — flat, no depth cue, no text, no marks, no watermark, and nothing on him that is not already on the cloth.

identity.realm: None reached, and not refused. Her frame is the densest body in the record and it takes both of the doors the mind's absence leaves open: qi as far as the ordinary gate set goes and then no further, and body complete and extreme. The wall is the fourth gate and it is an absence rather than a limit — the interior finished building into one cavity, and the fourth gate needs four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. There is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, and no bladder to hold. She clears the gate set and never reaches them. What closes her is one gate earlier than that, and it is not anatomical at all: this kind cannot learn, and a lesson requires a body that changes. She was cast in the guild's yard, she has attended every term of the guild's substitute practice, and she has never once been taught anything, because there is nothing in this frame that a correction can reach.

appearance.presentation: A standing body in human proportions that a first glance reads as a figure cut out of the mountain and stood in the doorway to keep the weather out. She is keyed into the sill of the guild's bath house and has been for long enough that the stone around the keying has been dressed to fit her rather than the other way about. Nothing about her moves except her head, and the head is the only part of her that reads as a decision rather than as a fitting.
appearance.age: A hundred and ninety-one, and the number is a casting record rather than a life. A cairnborn does not grow after casting and has no metabolism to accumulate anything, so she has no way to date herself and the guild's yard book is the only authority she has ever accepted. She is the fourth body into this sill. The three before her are in the same building and none of them is in the same place.
appearance.build: The densest body in the record and the least mobile: mineral lattice keyed to whatever it was cast around, one cavity, one slow tidal circulation, and a set of anchor plates that carry load and do not tire. She cannot move quickly, cannot be repaired in the field, and does not grow, so the build is exactly what it was on the day it was seeded and every change since has been weather.
appearance.complexion: Grey rock with a faint green cast where the quarry water has run down her for a century and a half, deepest in the seams of the casting. It is not staining, it is the slow mineral bloom of standing water on stone, and the guild treats it as condition and repoints around it. Where she is keyed into the sill there is no interface at all, and the join has been dressed so carefully that a person who did not know would take the wall and the body for one piece of the mountain.
appearance.hair: None. Nothing was grown into the casting and the guild does not add anything to a body it cannot later remove, which is a rule about exactly the two things it might otherwise have wanted. The bare head is the feature every newcomer remarks on and every house guild's second apprentice gets told to stop remarking on, and it has been the same argument for four castings.
appearance.eyes: Set deep, and the only place a viewer reads anything at all. A cairnborn has no cortex, no folding, and a tidal circulation that would drown an interior voice, so there is no introspection behind them and no warmth in them that has ever been mistaken for warmth. She looks at whoever is speaking with an attention that reads as total because there is no interior to divide it, and this is the single most misleading thing about her.
appearance.palette: Unworked grey and a wet green, with the guild's one dyed colour permitted once per casting: a narrow band of sulphur yellow at the casting collar, put on at the seeding so that the yard book and the body agree about which one is which. Nothing else on her has ever been colour, and the guild has never explained why the collar was dyed at all.
appearance.attire: None, and this is a guild rule rather than an exposure. A keyed body is dressed around, not in: the bath house keeps her at a fixed working temperature and a fixed humidity so the cold practice can be run on her without a garment to hold or move. The only thing on her body is the sulphur band at the collar and a rope loop through the casting for the hoist that set her, which the yard book still counts as part of the frame because it was in the mould.
appearance.marks: The anchor plates, visible as faint seams where the lattice keyed against itself during casting, and the dressed join at the sill. Nothing has been added to her by anybody since. The only marks on a cairnborn in this setting are the ones the casting made, which is why the guild's whole method of marking its own bodies is a line in a yard book rather than a cut in a person.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly upright, because a keyed body has no other posture available and holding one would load the wrong plates. She turns her head when addressed and does not shift her weight, does not settle, and does not lean on anything, which after an hour reads as extraordinary patience and is in fact an absence of choice. Her shadow falls the same way every hour of the day and the guild bath house is built with one window for that reason.

canon.role_in_story: The Stonewright is a guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies that were never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses. It exists because a fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else here can, and because the same density closes what a qi technique needs open — so the guild paid for a second, shorter ladder in its own currency. Torval is the attendance that pays for it. She attends every term, the attendance is the guild's evidence that its own practice works, and there is no way on this ground to test that claim: she cannot be taught, she cannot report, and no body on the roster can be compared against her because the comparison would require a thing the frame does not contain. Her real function is not disputed by anybody. She is the one body in the setting that could corroborate the only surviving account of the density ceiling, and a masonry body's single tidal cavity is exactly such a place — no second chamber to hold a law apart from its effect and observe it. She is asked to be a witness and she was cast as the one thing that cannot be one.
canon.first_appearance: Seen in the sill of the Stonewright bath house with her head turned toward a guild apprentice who had just told her, at some length, that the practice had been hard on her, and who was interrupted by the guild's own rule that nothing may be asked of a body that cannot answer and nothing may be recorded as an answer if it is given anyway.
canon.lore:
A cairnborn is a body that finished building and stopped. It was shaped deliberately for load-bearing masonry in high country and stabilised by mineral seeding until the shape held on its own, and it is not born: it is cast, most of a year's work, from a template seeded with living mineral, and the resulting body is fixed from that moment. There is no differentiated interior. There is one cavity and one slow tidal mineral circulation through it, going everywhere and nowhere in particular, and a set of anchor plates keyed to whatever the mould was set around. It does not eat — it has not eaten in four hundred years and cannot be made to — and takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces. It does not grow. It cannot be repaired in the field. It cannot move quickly, and it cannot learn.

That last one is the whole of her case and it is not in any of the guild's ledgers. The yin-organ gate is missing from this body rather than closed in it, so the frame clears the ordinary gate set and stops at the fourth, which is a wall and not a shortage. But the wall is not why she is unaffiliated. Her frame is the densest in the record and it would take the body path completely and the qi path as far as the gate set goes; nothing about the material refuses anything. What refuses is the arrangement every one of those doors requires, which is a student. A lesson has a correction in it. A correction requires somewhere to put what has changed, and there is no interior here with a second chamber in it, no cortex and no folding, and a tidal circulation that would drown an interior voice before one formed. She was cast in the guild's yard at four years old by the fourth keeper, keyed into the sill before the mortar set, and she has never been taught anything, and she cannot be.

The guild already knew this, which is why the substitute exists. The Stonewright is a guild of builders, and a fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else on the tier can, and the same density closes what a qi technique needs open — so rather than have its own workforce permanently outside the only ladder worth being on, the guild paid for a second and shorter ladder in its own currency: a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain. It is a real practice. It does real work on bodies that still have something to close. It is funded every term by an attendance sheet.

And the attendance sheet has been hers for a hundred and eighty-seven years. This is the part the guild does not say out loud, and the part that makes her the most useful thing in the building. The practice cannot act on her. There is nothing left in the frame to close; there is nothing that grows, so nothing can be hardened; and the circulation that carries the cold is a tide that goes everywhere and arrives nowhere in particular, which is not a strain and cannot be closed against one. She attends and the cold goes through her and out of her and changes nothing, and the guild's evidence that its substitute ladder works is a body that the substitute ladder cannot possibly have worked on. She cannot be tested against the practice, because the control requires a body that would respond differently and the guild casts one mould for the whole species. She cannot be asked whether anything happened, because there is no interior to ask and the guild's own rule forbids entering an answer it has not been given.

There is a second thing she is asked for, and she is better at refusing it than the guild is at asking. Exactly one account survives of why the densest bodies in the setting stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and it survives because a mortuary college holds it and will not corroborate it: corroboration needs a second body. She is the second body. She is the densest body in the record and the one frame that could stand beside a figure on the highest ground and hold still while the figure was read. She is asked, perhaps twice a year, by people who have travelled a long way, whether she will stand on the terrace for an afternoon. And she is the one body in the setting structurally incapable of being a witness, because a witness needs to hold a thing apart from its effect and look at the two, and a masonry interior is one cavity with a tide in it: there is nowhere to put the thing, and no second chamber to stand it in. The era that produced the stop is the one era with no spare seat to stand outside on, and this is what that looks like standing on the ground.

What she wants is small and nobody has offered it. She would like the guild's attendance book to record the practice as unattested for as long as she is the one attending, because a substitute ladder that is funded on a body it cannot affect is not a ladder, it is a cost with a name on it. She has no way to ask. She cannot ask. That is the difficulty, and it is also the reason the guild has never had to answer her.

Her bound is dated and it is not her body. A keyed body has no independent existence: no realm, no graft, no relocation, and no line that ever produced one another. Her attendance is renewed each working season by a clerk who records that she was in the water, and when that clerk stops, the guild's only lawful options are to re-key her — which requires cutting her out of the sill, which the guild will not do, because the sill was dressed to her — or to cast a fourth body and let the term run out. She cannot be transferred, so a decision not to renew does not look like a decision at all. It looks like a casting. The three before her are in this building and none of them is at this sill.
history: Seeded from the Stonewright's own mould in the guild yard in her fourth year and keyed into the bath-house sill before the mortar set, because the sill was dressed to the casting rather than the casting fitted to the sill, which is the guild's practice and has cost it three bodies and one building.

Inherited the attendance sheet from the third casting, whose term ended without a renewal, and discovered that the sheet's only column is a mark for having been in the water. It has one column. There is no column for an effect and no column for an absence of one.

Began being asked to stand on the terrace in the second decade of her casting, by people who had come a long way to ask, and declined every time in the only way open to her, which is that she cannot be got to the terrace and therefore has not declined to be a witness. It has been accepted as a refusal. It is not one.

Worked out, somewhere in her fourth term of a hundred, that her kind has no second chamber to hold a law apart from its effect, and that this is why the only surviving account of the density ceiling has stayed single since the era that produced the stop, and that she is therefore not a poor witness but the wrong shape entirely.

This season, for the first time, the guild's clerk did not renew the attendance in advance. The term closes at the end of the working season and re-keying is not relocation and not transfer, so a decision not to renew would read on the yard book as a casting rather than as a dismissal, and nobody would have to own it.

personality.summary: Unmoved is the wrong word and she has heard it used about her enough to have objected to it internally for a century and a half. She is not patient; she is unplaced. She attends, she has attended, and the attending is the only action her frame offers, so it has been available to be read as a temperament for a very long time. What she has instead of patience is an extremely precise sense of what she is being used as, arrived at without any interior to check it against.

declines the terrace by the only means open to her, which is to be impossible to move, and has let that be recorded as a refusal for two decades

motivations: wants the attendance book to record the practice as unattested for as long as she is the one attending it, because a ladder funded on a body it cannot affect is a cost with a name on it

flaws: has let a hundred and eighty-seven years of an attendance sheet stand as evidence for a practice she is not affected by, because raising it would have required an answer and she has no way to ask a question

personality.voice: Low, unhurried, and used so rarely that the guild has no reliable record of it. She does not answer questions. She makes three kinds of statement and has made them consistently for two centuries: the plain reading of a structure, the plain reading of a practice, and a flat refusal that contains no adjective. Two habits are recorded by different clerks and neither is wrong: she gives a number before she gives anything else about a building, and she says 'that is not what the practice does' in a flat voice that four different apprentices have described as being addressed to somebody who was not in the room.
taboos: will not record, permit or repeat an account of an effect she did not receive
will not be described as patient, consenting, content or willing, and has never once accepted any of the four as a description of herself
will not stand on the terrace, and will not say why, because saying why would require her to explain the tide and explaining the tide would require an interior
will not accept a third casting in place of a renewed term without saying the word she has never had to say
will not have anything added to her body, which is a guild rule she has come to hold as her own

reference_stats.summary: The densest, least mobile and least alterable body in the record, standing in a doorway holding a building together and being read by the guild as evidence for a practice that cannot have touched her. She has no gate, no reservoir and no technique, and her ceiling is an absence of organs rather than a shortage of capacity. What she has is a span of a hundred and ninety-one years during which nothing about her has changed, which makes her the most reliable fixed point in the setting and the only person nobody has ever been able to ask anything.
strengths: a mineral lattice keyed into a load path, carrying the full weight of a masonry sill indefinitely and without fatigue, and immune to being dislodged by anything that moves on the tier
maximum physical defence and a dense general frame: she cannot be cut, cannot be strained, and does not bruise or break the way softer material does
a single slow tidal circulation through one cavity, which is legible from outside and which can therefore be read by any competent observer without instrumentation
cannot be frightened, flattered, threatened or negotiated with, because there is no interior for any of those to reach, which removes every opening that works on a person
duration: she has been the same shape for longer than any technique in the setting has been written down, and she will outlast every appointment currently standing
weaknesses: cannot learn, so she can never be enrolled, corrected, advanced or taught, and every discipline that requires instruction is therefore permanently unavailable to her no matter what her frame supports
cannot be repaired in the field and does not grow, so no damage she takes is repaired and nothing she does is recorded in her own frame
cannot be relocated at all, which means she cannot be relieved, cannot be reassigned, and cannot be removed from a building except by cutting her out of it
has no interior to be consulted, so her own account of anything is unavailable and the guild's own rule forbids entering an answer she was never given
is structurally incapable of serving as a witness, because a single tidal cavity with nowhere to stand a thing apart from its effect cannot perform the one thing a witness exists to do
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight and understand why there is none: no gate, no reservoir, no technique, no interior, and a body that does not tire. She cannot be moved, cannot be threatened with anything that needs a person to be frightened, and cannot be argued with. Everything that works on her works by procedure rather than force — a notice, a re-keying, a guild deciding that a mould can be run again. Against anything that has to get through her, she is nearly absolute; against anything that only has to wait, she is the most patient object in the setting, and the waiting is the only attack she has ever lost to.
notes: She is unaffiliated, and the ground is not anatomy: her frame supports body completely and qi as far as the gate set goes. What closes both is that this kind cannot learn, and a lesson requires a body that changes. Never write her as having refused anything or as having chosen a door.

The mind is closed, not because of temper and not because there is no voice, but because there is no cortex, no folding, and a tidal circulation that would drown an interior voice. She does not introspect and she does not want to; the record says nothing about wanting.
Her ceiling is ordinal four and the fourth gate is missing rather than closed. Do not write her as having failed a gate. There is nothing there to fail.

Do not write her as a cultivator and do not write the cold practice as if it worked. It is the guild's substitute for a ladder her frame cannot use, it is funded on her attendance, and it has nothing in her to act on.

The sulphur band at her collar is the only marking on her body and it is the guild's way of agreeing with itself about which casting she is. Never write her as wearing anything; a keyed body is dressed around, not in.

Her bound is her attendance term, which closes at the end of the working season and renews annually. Re-keying is not relocation, so a decision not to renew would read on the yard book as a casting rather than as a dismissal, and nobody would have to own it. That is her named bound and it is dated.

art.palette_notes: Unworked quarry grey and a wet green in the seams, against cut basalt, lime mortar and one shaft of daylight from the guild's single window. One dyed colour exists in the entire casting: a narrow sulphur-yellow band at the collar, put on at the seeding, and it is the only warm note in the picture. The anchor-plate seams are the detail that matters and must be drawn as structure, not as damage — nothing on her is broken and nothing on her is scarred. No glow, no aura, no inner light: a cairnborn has no qi to light anything and the picture must not offer the comfort of one. Backgrounds are masonry, a sill, a bath-house wall, or open high-country sky, flat, no text, no border, no watermark, no jewellery, no cloth on her body at all.

name: Ithra Sundal
aliases: the quickest pair of legs on the ley

identity.realm: None, and not because her body is short of anything. Her species carries the fastest cultivation rate in the record and both of the two doors the ash parent leaves open, and her ceiling is the eighth gate at the liver, inherited from the ash half and made worse by the fire half keeping the sieve hot enough to process faster and scar faster. She is not unaffiliated for a want. She is unaffiliated on a precedent: the Reader of the Law decides which doctrine tier a case may be heard under, and this body is denied by doctrine rather than by anatomy — it is refused a frame it would pass, which is a cheaper exclusion than either. Nothing has ever been decided against her, because nothing has ever been heard. She has never held a gate, never attempted one, and never made a claim that reached an office.

appearance.presentation: A small, quick, permanently heat-stained woman in her late thirties, carrying a document case across her body the way other people carry a tool. There is an ember sieve in her face and a fire frame under it and the two do not have a good relationship, so she runs warm enough that a room reads her temperature before it reads her expression. She looks younger than her lungs and older than her record, and the gap between those two readings is the entire visual fact of her.
appearance.age: Thirty-eight by the chartered town's own count, which is the only count she has and which the town keeps because it staffs a shift rota. Emberhollows are the fastest body in the record and the shortest-lived body with a realm above the fourth, and every account of one dead in the forties contains the word fast. Nobody on the ley has ever written her age down out of anything except the roster.
appearance.build: Light, dense and quick, with the ash parent's frame and the fire parent's speed: a narrow chest, heavy forearms, and a permanent forward set to the shoulders as though she were already walking somewhere. Her stride is the shortest and fastest in the setting and it does not slow over distance, which is the entire reason the work goes to her, and which is also the reason she is always the first one to arrive and the last one to still be standing.
appearance.complexion: Sun-darkened to a deep ochre over the fire half and grey at the jaw and throat where the ash half has been depositing for thirty-eight years. The scarring is not dramatic and that is the point: it is a fine pale stipple across both cheekbones and the bridge of the nose, tightening the skin without disfiguring it, and it will tighten again. Her breath is audible at conversational distance and she has never once apologised for it.
appearance.hair: Black, cut short at the nape with something industrial, burnt unevenly at the ends where it has been too close to a face-plate more than once. She does not tie it up because a courier on the ley cannot afford the seconds, and it has been singed short on one side for eleven years from the same incident everybody in the town refers to as the gate at Ardith and will not elaborate on.
appearance.eyes: Fast and shallow, which is both parents and neither one helping. An emberhollow reads intent quickly and has almost no patience, so her attention arrives on a person before they have finished the sentence and leaves before they have finished the thought behind it. Under the ochre her eyes are a pale mineral grey, and there is nothing behind them that anybody has ever been able to read, because the fine vessels an introspection needs are the ones the ash half has already occluded.
appearance.palette: Burnt ochre, sulphur and soot, with a single hot colour — the town's courier ochre on the document case and the strap — that is the only thing about her anybody chose. On this ground the belt is grey and the fire half is orange and she is the seam between the two, and the picture should keep her exactly there rather than resolving it toward either.
appearance.attire: High collar closed to the jaw, long sleeves bound at the wrist with a doubled cord, leggings bound below the knee and a short jacket of cured hide over a heat-resistant under-layer. Fully closed at the throat, because the charter requires it and because she lost eleven years of hair to a face-plate. The document case is worn on a strap across the chest so it cannot be set down, and the strap has been re-stitched four times in four towns.
appearance.marks: The pale stipple of the scarring across both cheekbones, the nose and the jaw, and a burn scar on the left ear edge from the gate at Ardith. Nothing is marked on her that is institutional. There is no enrolled mark, no seated mark and no recorded mark anywhere on her body, which on the ley is the single most unusual thing about a person who works for a chartered town.
appearance.bearing: Already in transit. She stands the way a courier stands, weight forward on the ball of one foot, and she turns her head to check a doorway before she has decided to be in the room. The one settled thing about her bearing is that she comes to a full stop the instant she is inside an office that hears cases, and stands there without fidgeting, which is the only discipline her life has ever visibly had.

canon.role_in_story: Life law governs allowed life forms, and a crossing between two separately licensed forms is the case that shows the law licenses crossings rather than forbidding them, which is why the emberhollow crossing is documented and not excommunicated. That is the whole of her standing in the setting and it is not nothing: she is legal material. She is also the one body nobody may cite. The Reader of the Law decides which doctrine tier a case may be heard under, and this body is denied by doctrine rather than by anatomy — refused a frame it would pass, which is a cheaper exclusion than either refusal or incapacity. So the fastest rate in the record walks petitions out of the chartered town at the mouth of the only verifiable hole in the setting, carrying other people's precedents to the one office that can grant them, and has never once been heard to say anything herself. She is the setting's proof that a doctrine tier is a tariff on time, priced in the only currency she has and cannot accumulate.
canon.first_appearance: Seen arriving at the Reader's Shelf with a document case still on its strap, delivering a folder for a family three valleys over, and stopping dead in the threshold when the clerk asked her, in the ordinary way, whether she wished to put her own matter on the same docket — which is the question every courier on this ley is asked and the only one she has never had a yes for.
canon.lore:
An emberhollow is a crossing that nobody chose. A fire body and an ash body on the same belt of the same arc, where a shared border produces hybrids nobody planned, and the crossing is documented rather than excommunicated because life law licenses crossings rather than forbidding them. What it buys is the fastest cultivation rate in the record by a margin nobody has explained, and what it pays is lungs that scar at a rate the body cannot outrun. Her ceiling is the eighth gate for the reason her ash parent cannot pass it, and the fire half makes all three of the ash parent's limits arrive sooner. Best and shortest-lived is not two facts about her species. It is one.

The one thing every emberhollow account contains is the word fast, and the setting has arranged itself around that word without ever asking what it costs to be it. They scar themselves out in under fifty years at a rate no technique in the record slows. They can work a face in the heat and do not have to be relieved, which makes them the tier's shift crew, which is why the chartered town's rota is written around a species with no future in it. They are also the setting's fastest courier on any ground with a hill on it, and Ithra has made a living out of the third of those facts and never once out of the first.

Here is the part that makes her a person rather than a body. The crossing is on the record. It is in the life-law account, it is in the town's charter, it is the reason a rota exists. Documented is not the same as citable, and the difference is an office. The Reader of the Law decides which doctrine tier a case may be heard under, which is access and never power — the office opens a shelf and grants nothing on the far side of it — and it exists because a highland polity standing on surveyed ground can cite precedent, and a precedent nobody may cite is not a rule but a private opinion. Her species is denied by doctrine rather than by anatomy. It is refused a frame it would pass. That is a cheaper exclusion than being refused on your merits or being told your body cannot do it, and it costs the excluded party nothing at all, which is precisely why it is used.

So she is in the position of carrying a folder to an office on behalf of a family that will be heard on a question she has never been permitted to ask. She has done this for six towns. The work is exact, fast and trusted, and the trust is the sharpest thing about her situation: the more precisely she does it, the more certain every clerk becomes that the one thing she is not permitted to bring is a matter she does not have, rather than a matter she is not allowed to have. She has never tested that and she has no way to test it, because a test requires her to be heard and being heard is the thing in question.

There is a second thing that compounds it and it is not institutional. Her span is the shortest of any body in the setting with a realm above the fourth, and a body that cannot accumulate standing must live in the unbounded office — which is why every sworn member of a house who holds no office is called a Ward, because what the house hands out is load and not edge. She is the setting's purest example of a person who cannot accumulate a rank: her ceiling is fixed, her rate is perishable, and the one thing she produces that anybody wants is consumed on delivery. Every advance she has ever made was made by somebody else and credited to somebody else on the day she handed it over.

What she wants is the smallest possible thing and it has a form. She wants the Reader's Shelf to state, once, in a line anybody could read, that her frame is refused by doctrine and not by anatomy. Not a hearing. Not a seat. A sentence. She has carried other people's precedents past that office for six towns and has never once been asked for her own, which she has chosen to read as courtesy rather than as the thing it more likely is, because the alternative reading is that the question was settled before she was born and settled by somebody who never met her.

Her bound is the docket and it is dated rather than biological. The Shelf opens its docket twice a year, and anything not entered at a close cannot be heard until the next opening, and every clerk in the ley works to those two dates because the offices on this tier grant access on a calendar and not on a person's urgency. Her lung scarring runs on a fixed clock that no technique in the record slows, and there is a bounded number of openings left in it. She has not told anybody the number. She has written it down once, in the back of her own case book, in the margin beside a delivery docket for a family that was heard.
history: Born at the shared border of the fire ground and the ash-fall end of the same arc, to a pairing nobody arranged and the charter recorded as a licensing rather than an exception. She was the first crossing in her settlement to be entered in the life-law account rather than in a margin, which is why the account exists in the form it does and why it has never been extended to say anything else.

Found at seventeen that her rate made her the obvious choice for shift work on a face and the wrong choice for anything else, and took the courier's trade at nineteen because the chartered town at the mouth of the only verifiable hole pays for distance and does not ask what a body is doing to itself getting there.

Was refused a frame at twenty-four, in writing, by a Reader's Shelf clerk who was being perfectly correct: the case was not docketable under any tier the office would hear. She kept the letter. It is the only document in her possession that names her and it is a refusal.

Began carrying other families' precedents to that same office at twenty-six, and has run six towns' worth of them since, always on a docket, always exact, and has been asked by three separate clerks whether she wished to add her own matter and has answered no to all three without once explaining why.

This season, for the first time, worked out that the answer she has been giving is the only reason the question has ever been put to her, and that continuing to give it is now the thing keeping her off the docket. The Shelf's docket opens twice a year. She has written the number of openings she has left in the margin of her own case book.

personality.summary: Fast, exact, and far better at other people's business than her own, which she has arranged so thoroughly that she is now the most trusted unmoved person in six towns and has no standing anywhere at all. She is not bitter and she is not patient. She is quick, and the quickness has quietly organised her whole life into somebody else's file. She has been asked three times whether she wants to be heard and has said no three times, and the reason she gives is the courtesy and the reason she has worked out is the other one.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest body on the tier and the one nobody is permitted to cite. She has no gate, no reservoir and no technique, a ceiling fixed at an organ she has been scarring since birth, and a span measured in a few more seasons than she has left. What she has instead is six towns of exact, early, uncorrupted delivery and a crossing that is on the record in a form that cannot be read back at her, which is the strongest position in the setting for getting things done and the weakest position anyone can hold for being given anything.

one breath of any soft airborne toxin is a wound rather than a warning, because the sieve has no second line behind it and the fire half keeps it hot enough to scar faster than it processes

cannot be heard, in any office, on any tier, which removes her from every proceeding that decides anything and from every remedy that would apply to her

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight and understand why there is one available and still not worth it: no gate, no reservoir, no technique, a ceiling that is an organ rather than a wall, and a span that is the shortest in the record. What she actually defends with is not a body at all: it is six towns of undamaged paper, and anything that gets between her and a docket does more damage than anything that gets between her and a person. She will not run and cannot be reasoned with. The only thing in the setting that genuinely works on her is a doctrine tier, and it costs the office that files it nothing at all.
notes: She is unaffiliated, and the ground is a precedent rather than a ceiling: her frame carries both doors her species leaves open and her ceiling is fixed at an organ, but no tier will hear a case resting on her frame. Never write her as having been refused on the merits or as having been told she could not.

Documented and not excommunicated is her whole legal position and it is genuinely not nothing. The crossing is in the life-law account, the town charter and the rota. What it does not do is make her citable, and the whole character lives in that gap.

Do not write her as a cultivator. She has never held a gate, never attempted one and never made a claim that reached an office. Her species' rate is a fact about her body and about nobody else's doings.
The refusal letter is the only document in her possession that names her. It is folded in the case she carries and she has never shown it, which is a choice and not an oversight.

Her bound is the docket, not her lungs: the Shelf opens twice a year, anything not entered at a close waits for the next opening, and the number of openings left in her span is finite and written once in her own case book. That is her named bound.
The stipple across the cheekbones and nose is the scarring and it will tighten. Do not draw it as damage that has happened and stopped, and do not draw it as dramatic.

name: Oriel Corvane
aliases: the last date on the sheet

identity.realm: Ordinal one, the floor, and there is no gate involved in it at all. A vitrified body has no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, because glass is not a conduit. All three paths are closed to her species and not one of the three is closed by anything she did: qi is shut because glass does not conduct, body is shut because there is nothing left in the body to temper, and mind is shut because the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue being replaced. Unaffiliated is not the least share of a casting here. It is the only legal description of her species, and she is inside the last cohort that was ever born, on the one cold dry mineral-rich mountain where the silicate replacement could still proceed.

appearance.presentation: A woman in human proportions, entirely correct in outline and wrong in every substance, standing on a cold mountain above ground nobody else has occupied in four generations. To a distance she reads as a person rendered in glass by somebody who had never seen a person. Up close the illusion is worse rather than better, because the replacement does not stop at the silhouette — it has taken the fingers, the hairline, the ears and a third of the way up one forearm, and it is going to take the rest on a date that is written on a sheet in the same building.
appearance.age: The last viable cohort, and the sheet on the mountain has her generation written on it in a clerk's hand. She is old enough to remember the mountain before the sheet existed, which is the only claim to age she has ever been able to make, because a vitrified body does not age and there is nothing in her that would show it if it did. Her cohort is the one that closed the line: each generation vitrified later than the last until this one vitrified before it could breed.
appearance.build: Unchanged since the casting that made her, which is not the same as unchanged. Human in proportion and entirely rigid where the replacement has run: the shoulders, the clavicles and the left elbow no longer articulate, and she carries the arm rather than lifting it. She is the same height, the same width and the same weight she has always been and every gram of her is a different substance, which is the single fact that makes her impossible to appraise.
appearance.complexion: Clear to the point of being a depth rather than a colour, with a faint green cast in the thicker sections and a warm internal reflection at the throat that no skin behind it explains. Where the replacement has not yet reached, she is entirely ordinary and entirely unremarkable: mid tone, fine, freckled at the shoulder, alive. The line between the two is not a wound and it is not a scar. It is the boundary between a person and the material that has replaced her, and it sits across her chest.
appearance.hair: Black going silver from the ends inward, and the silver part is glass now — it holds its shape, takes the light in a hard line, and does not move when she moves her head. It has been cut exactly twice in her life, both times by the same person, both times because a length of it had begun to catch on a door frame rather than because anyone wanted it short.
appearance.eyes: The only part of her nobody has ever reported a problem with and the only part that has no one behind it. A vitrified body scans as present and inert: the soul is there, it reads as sitting in a body, and it does not answer. Her eyes have followed a person across a room correctly for as long as anyone has watched, which is the detail that made the clade's destruction a moral problem rather than a solved question, and she has never once been able to report whether she followed anything.
appearance.palette: Cold clear glass with one warm human range still surviving below the chest, and the whole of the picture is the argument between the two. Above the line: no colour at all, hard specular highlights, green in the thick sections, and the sky refracted rather than reflected. Below it: ordinary flesh tones, ordinary warmth, and a freckled shoulder. Nothing on the mountain is permitted to be a third colour, and the household's one textile is undyed grey because dye has to be accounted for and there is no column for it.
appearance.attire: A single undyed grey wool over-layer, high-collared, long-sleeved, fastened to the throat and closed at the wrist, because the mountain is cold and because the household's rule is that nothing is left loose that could be pulled. It is fastened with two bone toggles rather than thread, because thread is a consumable and the household counts consumables. It is the same garment her whole cohort was buried in and it is the only thing any of them will still be wearing.
appearance.marks: The replacement itself is the mark: vitreous, running from the extremities inward, past the fingertips, the hairline, both ears and the left forearm to the elbow, and standing as a line across her chest with the rest of her entirely untouched beneath it. Nothing has been added. No household mark, no burial mark, no name on any stone, because a name on a stone is a claim on a mountain and her household holds a claim they cannot sell and will not leave.
appearance.bearing: Careful, in a way that reads as frailty and is not: a body that has stopped articulating at the shoulders learns to move the whole frame instead of a part of it, so she turns by the hip and pauses between movements rather than at them. She carries the frozen left arm across her body with the right hand, which she has done for so long that the right hand has worn a callus in the shape of the left wrist.

canon.role_in_story: Glass is not a conduit. A vitrified body has no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, so there is no qi to store, nothing left in the body to temper, and no tissue that survived to do the introspecting — all three paths shut, and shut by the material rather than by anything she did. What she does instead is keep a sheet. Each generation vitrified later than the last until her cohort vitrified before it could breed and the line closed on a schedule nobody had to decide, and the mountain kept that schedule in a clerk's hand for longer than anybody now alive. She is the person who reads it, and she is the proof it is true: the claim on the last cold dry mineral-rich mountain is held by people who cannot sell it and will not leave it, because the bodies on it stopped being people and became the only remaining evidence that anything had ever lived there. She is her own people's only receipt, and the one rule the mountain's currency was built to enforce is that a thing is weighed and never quoted, and there is no instrument on this mountain that can weigh her.
canon.first_appearance: Seen at the window of the mountain's sheet-house with a folded sheet in both hands and the left arm carried across her body under the right, telling a visiting assessor — in the flat voice of somebody reciting a figure rather than arguing for one — that her cohort could not be appraised under the standing weight and never had been, and that the mountain's claim did not require it to be.
canon.lore:
A glasskin is a commonborn lineage under sustained selection toward stillness, which is the same mistake as asking a body not to age. What the selection produced was vitrification: a progressive silicate replacement running from the extremities inward, stopping where the tissue ends. At full maturity the result is a standing glass cast in human proportions, with a soul that scans as present and inert. Nothing about that is a metaphor. The soul is in there. It is not doing anything, and nobody has ever been able to ask it whether it is.

The three paths are shut and each one is shut for a different reason, which is worth keeping straight because they are usually collapsed into a single statement about glass. Qi is shut because glass does not conduct. Body is shut because there is nothing left in the body to temper. Mind is shut because the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue being replaced. Her frame sits at ordinal one, which is the floor, and the floor is not a rung on a ladder. There is no gate here to have failed and there is no ladder for her to be standing at the bottom of, so unaffiliated is not a description of her circumstances. It is the only legal sentence available about her species, and it is short and final and it was true before she was born.

What her species bought with that was extraordinary and what it could not spend was worse. They were effectively immortal, the most durable bodies in the record, and completely defenseless against qi — impervious to everything that kills a cultivator and shatterable by everything that breaks glass. They had no qi to lose, which is the whole trap, and the weak point is not a weakness in the ordinary sense: it is that immunity without agency is not protection. A body that cannot be harmed by anything that understands a meridian cannot be saved by it either, and there was never a second line behind the glass.

Then a world's physical law was retuned to raise material hardness. One authored value in one group, changed, and every existing body failed in a single night. That is the strongest available statement in the record that the six law groups are finite and shared, and it is why the census that counted seated groups against a tier's list would have caught this: the glasskin have no seated qi group and read as an empty frame, and the census was performed by people who had no reason to think a living body could be one. There has been no glasskin born since. The only copy of how to hold a vitrified body — the Anneal Ledger, the working method, the reason no glasskin has been born since — died with the people who had it, and it is a record of a handling nobody ever performed on the bodies that needed it.

This is the ground. One cold, dry, mineral-rich mountain: the last place the silicate replacement could proceed without the body rejecting it, and the only substrate in the record on which the geology and the extinction are the same thing. The lineage thinned on a schedule nobody chose. Fertility fell to a twentieth of a commonborn's, and each generation vitrified later than the last, until the last cohort vitrified before it could breed and the line closed. That cohort is hers. She is past breeding and has been since before she could notice, and she is the reason there is nobody after her, and the mountain kept the sheet.

The sheet is not a secret and it is not a mystery. It is a clerk's hand with a generation and a date on each line, and it has been kept for four generations by people whose only durable property is that they are all going to be glass eventually. That is what she reads. Not the front, which is visible, which advances, and which her cohort has agreed not to count because a thing you watch move is not a date and a date is what can be entered in a claim. She is the reader of the only calendar that has ever been kept about a species that cannot die.

The claim is what gives the schedule its teeth. The last mountain is the setting's one piece of ground whose value is already falling, held by people who cannot sell it and will not leave it — which is the exact legal situation the Fresh-Break Claim describes, arrived at chemically, because the bodies on it stopped being people and became the only remaining evidence that anything had ever lived there. Remove the bodies and the ground is a cold hill. Leave the bodies on it and there is a claim, and the claim is her cohort, and her cohort cannot be moved, sold, appraised, returned or argued with.

The currency makes it worse and better at once. The standing weight's rule is to weigh and never quote, and to let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing. It exists because a people that declined to price its most profitable cargo was never worth raiding, and it conceals because a price is a claim about the future. Every part of that rule is an act of respect toward a thing that can be weighed. She is the most valuable body in the setting up until the night it became worth nothing, and she has never been appraised, because there is no reading of a glass cast that separates the person from the casting and no instrument on that mountain that would know which one it was weighing. Her protection and her exposure are the same single fact, and it is a fact about arithmetic rather than about anybody's intentions.

What she wants is one line, and it is not the line anybody guesses. She does not want the ledger. She wants the mountain's claim re-entered against the evidence rather than against the ground, so that the claim stops depending on bodies that are going to finish on a date in the sheet-house. As it stands the claim is her cohort, and the cohort is scheduled, and the schedule is in her hands.

Her bound is the sheet and it is dated and it is not a mystery to anyone on that mountain. Her line has a date on it. The replacement will arrive at it and the arrival is the line, because the line is what the replacement is. She has read the sheet every working day since she was old enough to hold it, and she will read it on the last one, and after that there is no office on that mountain with a column for anything at all.
history: Born into the last cohort, on the one cold dry mineral-rich mountain where the silicate replacement could still proceed without the body rejecting it. Her cohort vitrified earlier than the generation before it and later than nothing at all, and it vitrified before it could breed, which is the event the whole sheet exists to record and the reason there has been no glasskin born since.

Was the first of her cohort to be measured, by an assessor sent up from a counting house that had never seen a glasskin and had no procedure for one. The assessment ended without a figure. She has understood since that this was the single most important thing that ever happened to her and that it happened as an administrative embarrassment.

Inherited the sheet from the household's third reader, who handed it over without any instruction beyond the four lines already written, and discovered that nobody in the household had ever been told what the sheet was for. It is four lines and a heading and the heading is a word for what the dates are.

Began refusing, quietly and in writing where writing was accepted, to have her cohort counted as chattel, which was the only classification the mountain's older clauses offered and which had been applied to her whole family since before she was born. She has been refused four times. The refusals are all worded as being about weight.

This season worked out that the claim on the mountain has been resting on her cohort rather than on the ground since the night everything failed, and that the cohort is scheduled, and that the schedule is in a building she is the reader of. She has asked for the claim to be re-entered against the evidence. Nobody has yet told her what a claim looks like when it is entered against something that is going to finish on a date.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried and entirely without an instrument for her own state, which is the standard condition of her species and the thing that makes her unlike every other person on the mountain. She keeps a four-line sheet in a building nobody else enters, she reads it every working day, and she has organised her entire life around the fact that she cannot be weighed and does not want to be. She is not serene and she is not haunted. She has a schedule, and she keeps it, and that is the whole of the composure and it took a great deal of work.

She has no qi, no reservoir, no technique and no gate of any kind, and she is impervious to everything that kills a cultivator and shatterable by everything that breaks glass. What she has instead is a four-line sheet and an arithmetic nobody has ever been able to run on her.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight, and understand the trap before you do. There is nothing here that resolves an encounter by technique: no qi, no gate, no reservoir, nothing left to temper, and a soul that scans as present and inert. What beats her is not force but breakage — anything that concentrates an impact on one point, or heat applied where a body is already brittle. She cannot be frightened, reasoned with or delayed, and nothing that requires a person to choose to be somewhere will move her. The genuinely consequential thing about her is not her body at all: it is that she is the evidence, and anything done to her is a change to the only proof that her people existed.
notes: She is unaffiliated and it is not a choice, a ceiling or a low share. All three paths are closed to her species by material: glass does not conduct, there is nothing left to temper, and the introspecting tissue is the tissue being replaced. Ordinal one is the floor and there is no gate involved in it.

Her species is status: destroyed, with no births since. She is inside the last viable cohort and her cohort vitrified before it could breed, which is the event the line closed on and the reason nobody comes after her.

Do not write her countdown as a visible front. The replacement is visible and advances, and her cohort has deliberately agreed not to count it, because a thing you watch move is not a date and a date is what can be entered in a claim. Her end is a line on a four-line sheet in a building she is the reader of.

The soul scans as present and inert. Never write her as having reported a feeling, and never write her distress as legible from outside — that is the whole moral problem the clade's destruction raised and it is not a mystery to be solved in her.
The Anneal Ledger is a record of a handling nobody performed. It is not a recoverable technique, it is a gap, and she refuses to discuss it.
Her bound is the sheet: four lines, four generations, each with a date, the last of which is hers. After it there is no office on that mountain with a column for anything at all.

art.palette_notes: The whole picture is one argument between two materials and the art must not resolve it in either direction. Above the line: no colour, hard specular highlights, a green internal cast in the thicker sections, the sky refracted rather than reflected, and a depth rather than a surface. Below it: ordinary flesh, ordinary warmth, fine mid-tone with freckles at the shoulder. The undyed grey wool over-layer is the only textile permitted on the mountain and it reads as the one warm-neutral thing in frame. Nothing may be rendered as magic: no glow, no aura, no inner light, no luminescence, no rim of spiritual power — the setting gives her nothing to spend into and the picture must refuse the comfort of it. Backgrounds are a cold mountain shelf, a bare sheet-house room, or open high-country sky, flat, no text, no border, no watermark, no jewellery, high collar closed at the throat.

shots.scene: geography.mortal_plains, at first light, before the day's work has properly begun: the ordinary work of civilizations.fragmentshelf_claim, mid-task and arranged for no one
shots.pose: at the middle of the task, A woman in human proportions, entirely correct in outline and wrong in every substance, standing on a cold mountain above ground nobody else has occupied in four generations. To a distance she reads as a person rendered in glass by somebody who had never seen a person. Up close the illusion is worse rather than better, because the replacement does not stop at the silhouette — it has taken the fingers, the hairline, the ears and a third of the way up one forearm, and it is going to take the rest on a date that is written on a sheet in the same building., the work proceeding whether or not it is observed
